modules.name: Occupancy classification and fire-safety assumptions (shared upstream node)
modules.design_question: Which major occupancy and sprinkler status does each storey carry, as one shared input to the egress, high-building, accessibility and energy-limit checks?
modules.effort: S: about 2 person-days (13 Nov cut: mapping table, locked sprinkler flag, area by occupancy, edition stamp)
inputs: Layer 0: program tags and area per storey
Layer 0: height of top-storey floor above grade
Layer 0: below-grade transit concourse and parking tags
User entry: alternative-solution request to omit sprinklers (flagged, not a default)

Edition stamp for downstream clause checks

parameters.name: Program tag to major occupancy mapping
parameters.unit: group and division (A-1 to A-4, C, D, E, F-3)
parameters.relationship: Editable table per Table 3.1.2.1: office D, retail E, residential and hotel C, performing arts A-1, other assembly A-2, parking F-3, concourse by consultant. Group sets separations, occupant-load factors, travel limits and Part 10 rows.

parameters.name: Multiple major occupancies rule
parameters.relationship: The most restricted occupancy governs the whole building (3.2.2.6); superimposed occupancies follow their own portion (3.2.2.7); occupancies under 10% of a storey area may be ignored (3.2.2.8). Tag mix changes construction and separations.

parameters.name: Sprinkler status per storey
parameters.relationship: Locked to 'required': every new building is sprinklered to NFPA 13 (3.2.2.18.(3), 3.2.5.12) and the any-height articles require sprinklers throughout. An 'off' entry is an alternative solution and would cut travel limits to 30 or 40 m.

parameters.name: Height of top-storey floor above grade
parameters.relationship: Measured to the uppermost floor level of the top storey; above 18 m the 3.2.6 measures and 3.2.7.9 emergency power apply. A 244-305 m tower is far above it, so downstream modules read this value only.

metrics.name: Floor area assigned to a major occupancy
metrics.good: green: 100
metrics.basis: [applicability: team] Process check: unclassified area cannot be tested by P11-M04, M05, M06 or M07.

metrics.name: Sprinkler assumption recorded and stamped
metrics.good: green: 'required' with clause stamp
metrics.bad: red: switched off without an alternative-solution entry
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] r1 offered an 'off' switch; VBBL 2019 3.2.2.18.(3) requires sprinklers in every new building. Check VBBL 2025.
metrics.method: field present and equal to required

Not computed: subsidiary-occupancy review and transit-concourse classification.

Mapping table with source badges and edition stamp

modules.name: Lift traffic sizing and zoning by use
modules.design_question: How many lifts, of what size and speed, in how many rises, serve each use at acceptable service, and how much total core area (passenger plus service) results?
modules.effort: L: about 14-16 person-days in total. 13 Nov cut about 6: equal-floor up-peak RTT with express term, HC5 and interval gauges, one unit test (Peters example). Service-lift layer, population templates and rise diagram follow by 10 Dec; SimPy is roadmap (15+).
inputs: Layer 0: area per storey by program tag; unit counts by bedroom type; hotel room count
Layer 0: floor-to-floor heights (unequal allowed), storey count, main-lobby and below-grade transit levels
Core footprint and shaft availability from the massing/core module
User presets: density or persons per unit and room, utilisation, car library entry, speed, acceleration, jerk, door times, control type, traffic profile
User entries: transit mode share, station peak flow, escalator or shuttle capacity
Service-lift presets: firefighter, stretcher, goods, parking lifts
outputs: LiftGroupSpec[] (rise, floors served, express floors, cars, rated load, speed, traffic profile)
VTPerformance {RTT, HC5 %, interval per group; AWT and ATTD badged 'simulation not performed'}
CoreAreaByLevel {passenger shafts, service and firefighter shafts, lobbies, pits and overruns} separately and as total
NetToGross per typical level, computed from total core
RegulatoryFlags {seismic, single-run rise, sway, stack effect, regulator acceptance}

parameters.name: Population basis by use
parameters.unit: m2 NIA per person; persons per unit; persons per room
parameters.relationship: Office: area / density x utilisation. Residential and hotel: persons per unit (1.5 to 4.0 by bedrooms) or per room. More people add cars and shafts. Default 1 per 10 m2 is a team assumption; 1 per 8 is a London buffer.

parameters.name: Floors per rise (zone height)
parameters.relationship: More floors per rise adds probable stops and flight time, lengthening round-trip time and cutting capacity per car; more rises cut core area per rise but add transfer floors.

parameters.name: Rated speed, acceleration and jerk
parameters.relationship: Faster cars shorten flight time, so taller rises use higher speeds to hold round-trip times; on long express runs the speed profile sets real run time. Gains shrink when door and loading time dominate.

parameters.name: Car rated load and platform area
parameters.relationship: Larger cars carry more per trip, raising capacity per shaft but lengthening loading and enlarging the shaft. EN 81 pairs (1600 kg/21 persons) are placeholders; Canadian cars follow CSA B44. Table values not retrieved.

parameters.name: Control type (collective vs destination)
parameters.relationship: Destination control groups passengers by floor, cutting stops; its benefit must be shown by simulation, so v1 reports calculation results only.

parameters.name: Use zoning (separate groups by use)
parameters.relationship: Separate groups for basement, residential, hotel, office and public shuttles keep mixed traffic out of the main group, protecting its capacity at the cost of more shafts.

parameters.name: Lowest terminal (below-grade transit entrance)
parameters.relationship: A terminal below the main lobby adds a long first flight and stops to every round trip; a dedicated group or escalators keep it off the main group. Hoistways passing the lowest exit storey need vestibules or seals (3.2.6.2.(4)).

parameters.name: Utilisation factor (share of floor population present at peak)
parameters.relationship: Scales design population; 22 Bishopsgate used 80%, so a lower factor trims lifts but risks under-provision if tenants over-occupy.

parameters.name: Express-zone run (unserved floors below a rise)
parameters.relationship: Floors a rise skips below its first served floor add twice the express run time to every round trip, so upper rises of a 244-305 m tower need higher speed or more cars. The classic formula omits this term.

parameters.name: Average car load P
parameters.relationship: P is average passengers per trip, about 80% of capacity in hand estimates and calculated in general analysis. Higher P raises HC5 per car but lengthens loading; rated capacity must not be used as P.

parameters.name: Traffic profile (up-peak, two-way, lunch)
parameters.relationship: Each profile changes which stops and directions count, so a gauge is valid only for its profile. v1 computes up-peak; two-way and lunch templates are roadmap.

parameters.name: Service and firefighter lifts
parameters.relationship: Firefighter, stretcher, goods and parking lifts add shafts, lobbies, pits and overruns that passenger counts omit; each storey with lift access needs one stretcher car (3.5.4.1). Counts are editable presets.

parameters.name: Transit mode share and station peak flow
parameters.relationship: User-entered mode share and station flow set demand at the below-grade terminal; escalator or shuttle capacity then sizes a separate group so these riders stay off the main group. No TransLink figures sourced.

parameters.name: Seismic, wind, rope-length and stack-effect constraints
parameters.relationship: BC requires CSA B44-16; its seismic clause, post-earthquake lift availability, rope sway and single-run rise can cap rise height and speed. Appendix C context: Sa(0.2) 0.848, PGA 0.369, wind 1/50 0.45 kPa.

metrics.name: Up-peak 5-minute handling capacity (office)
metrics.good: green: HC5 >= 13
metrics.basis: [applicability: institutional + project_example] UQ DS-11 target 13% (Australia); Peters worked example 12% (UK practice). Not a Canadian code limit. Profile: up-peak.
metrics.method: HC5 = 300 x P x N / RTT / population x 100, P = average car load

metrics.name: Up-peak average interval (office)
metrics.good: green: interval <= 30
metrics.basis: [applicability: institutional + project_example] UQ: under 30 s; Peters example: 30 s. Profile: up-peak.

metrics.name: Up-peak average waiting time (office, all floors served)
metrics.good: green: AWT <= 25
metrics.bad: red: AWT > 30, or AWT > 25 with ATTD > 80; amber: 25 < AWT <= 30 with ATTD <= 80
metrics.basis: [applicability: uk_guidance] BCO 2014 quoted second-hand by Stopes; later editions unchecked. v1 badge: simulation not performed; estimate AWT = interval / 2.
metrics.method: v1: AWT = interval / 2; roadmap: Monte Carlo simulation

metrics.name: Up-peak average time to destination (office)
metrics.good: green: ATTD <= 90
metrics.bad: red: ATTD > 110, or ATTD > 90 with AWT >= 25; amber: 90 < ATTD <= 110 with AWT < 25
metrics.basis: [applicability: uk_guidance] BCO 2014 quoted by Stopes; superseded-edition check pending. The project targeted 30 s and 80 s. v1 badge: simulation not performed.
metrics.method: Roadmap: simulated waiting plus ride time

metrics.name: Residential two-way handling capacity and interval
metrics.good: green: HC >= 8 and interval <= 40 (UQ band, default); amber: HC >= 7 and interval <= 60
metrics.basis: [applicability: institutional + project_example] Green is UQ DS-11 (8%, under 40 s); amber floor is Arup 505 George St citing CIBSE Guide D (7%, 50-60 s). Default is the stricter band. Profile: two-way. v1 badge: not computed until template validated.

metrics.name: Hotel, cultural, observation and public-use traffic criteria
metrics.good: set by designer
metrics.basis: [applicability: team] No sourced criteria found; editable preset with its traffic profile named.

metrics.name: Floors per single-deck rise
metrics.good: green: floors <= 15
metrics.basis: [applicability: uk_guidance] CIBSE Guide D as cited by Peters. Arup's 21-28 floor fast residential rises make this a review flag, not a ban.

metrics.name: Net-to-gross area ratio (NIA/GIA), typical floor
metrics.good: green: NTG >= 75
metrics.basis: [applicability: uk_guidance] UK practitioner statement (Stopes); Canadian measurement conventions differ. Computed from total core (passenger plus service, firefighter, lobbies).
metrics.method: NIA / GIA after subtracting total core, lobbies and shafts

metrics.name: Passenger-shaft share of floor plate by level
metrics.good: lowest option that meets all gauges above
metrics.basis: [applicability: project_example] Report-only comparison; no sourced threshold. Peters counts passenger shafts only.
metrics.method: sum of passenger shaft footprints at level / floor plate area

metrics.name: Total lift core area vs passenger-only area
metrics.good: report both; no threshold
metrics.bad: total omitted or equal to passenger-only
metrics.basis: [applicability: project_example] Passenger-only figures flatter net-to-gross; total adds service lifts, lobbies, pits and overruns from presets.
metrics.method: passenger shafts + service shafts + lobbies + pits and overruns

metrics.name: Stretcher-capable car provided
metrics.good: green: every storey with lift access has at least one car taking a 2010 x 610 mm stretcher, identified at the main entrance level
metrics.bad: red: none on any such storey
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 3.5.4.1 agree; waived for limited-use or limited-application elevators. VBBL 2025 unread.

metrics.name: Transit-level peak demand vs shuttle or escalator capacity
metrics.good: user target
metrics.basis: [applicability: team] No sourced flows or escalator capacity; user enters station peak flow and mode share.
metrics.method: tower population at the level x mode share vs capacity

modules.method: 1) Population per level: office area / density x utilisation; residential and hotel by persons per unit or room. 2) Group floors into rises by use and height; add a group for transit levels. 3) Per rise, RTT by general analysis: kinematic flight times per floor interval, express-zone run 2 x tx, stops S and reversal floor H from floor populations, door and transfer times, P = average car load; the classic 2H*tv + (S+1)*ts + 2P*tp is the equal-floor case. 4) HC5 = 300 x P x N / RTT / population; interval = RTT / N; pick the smallest N meeting the bands. 5) Core area = passenger plus service, firefighter and stretcher lifts, lobbies, pits, overruns, separately and in total. 6) Unit-test against the Peters worked example and the Arup rises (levels 4-25, 26-46, 47-74 at 3.5, 5.0, 6.0 m/s) before any gauge shows pass/fail.
visualization: Rise diagram: storeys vertical, one column per rise, solid = served, hatched = express, T = transfer floor, beside a 3D tower section
Gauge bars for HC5 and interval with green, amber and red bands, source badge, applicability badge and traffic-profile label; AWT and ATTD greyed 'simulation not performed'
Stacked core plans at ground, mid and top levels with passenger shafts, service lifts and lobbies in separate colours
Group specification table (cars, rating, speed, floors served)
modules.human_judgment: Tenant density and utilisation, acceptable waiting for each use, transfer acceptability, public-use traffic assumptions, final lift selection and simulation by a vertical-transportation consultant.
modules.limits: v1 is up-peak only; two-way, lunch, down-peak and SimPy dispatch are roadmap. Guidance is UK/Australian, not Canadian code. Guide D is paywalled. Peters 2000 unread. Early estimate, not certification.

modules.name: Lift strategy comparator: sky lobby, double-deck, destination control
modules.design_question: Which lift strategy (single-deck rises, sky lobby with shuttles, then double-deck and destination control) minimises total core area while keeping accessible, secure public-use floors high in the tower?
modules.effort: M: about 5 person-days for the single-deck and sky-lobby comparison on top of P11-M01; 10 Dec release, not in the 13 Nov cut. Double-deck and destination dispatch are roadmap (15+).
inputs: LiftGroupSpec[] and VTPerformance from P11-M01
Layer 0: storey heights and floor-use tags, including public or cultural floors high in the tower
Candidate sky-lobby and transfer floors
Structural core constraints from the structure module
User switches: direct-travel preference, public sky-room intent, security separation for public floors
outputs: StrategyOptionTable {total core m2, shafts at ground, transfers per typical trip, floor-height constraints}
SelectedStrategy flag for P11-M03 and P11-M05
FirefighterLiftReach {changes, run time, 'requires AHJ agreement' tag}

parameters.name: Strategy type
parameters.relationship: Double-deck halves possible stops and puts two cabs per shaft; sky lobbies drop express zones from upper rises, usually saving more core than shuttles add. v1 compares single-deck and sky lobby.

parameters.name: Floor-to-floor height uniformity
parameters.relationship: Double-deck cabs serve adjacent floors together, so every served floor needs equal height; double-height public floors then need escalators, separate lifts or adjustable-spacing cabs.

parameters.name: Transfers per journey (design-intent switch)
parameters.relationship: Sky lobbies force two-lift trips; London tenants demanded direct travel, steering 22 Bishopsgate to double-deck. VTC public floors high in the tower may favour sky lobbies as public rooms, so this is a switch.

parameters.name: Sky-lobby position and shuttle design
parameters.relationship: A top-down shuttle to the top of one local group is core-efficient but sends some riders up then down; shuttling to the lowest floor of each group is intuitive but needs more core.

parameters.name: Firefighter elevator continuity and run time
parameters.relationship: One firefighter elevator must reach every above-grade floor served with at most one change and a 1 min run to the top floor it serves (VBBL 2007 and 2019), so zoning, sky lobbies and 300 m height constrain it.

parameters.name: Recall to firefighter entrance or transfer lobby
parameters.relationship: Under emergency power every elevator must recall within 5 min from its most remote storey to the firefighter entrance or a transfer lobby (3.2.7.9.(3)); sky lobbies shorten runs and, if met, waive simultaneous operation.

parameters.name: Magnet floors (observation, restaurant, public cultural)
parameters.relationship: These concentrate trips on a few floors; dedicated high-speed shuttles (8.0 m/s at 22 Bishopsgate) keep them off the main groups but add shafts.

parameters.name: Destination control
parameters.relationship: Raises up-peak capacity and cuts non-coincident stops; confirm by simulation where average waiting time must not exceed 80% of the nominated interval (UQ rule). Manufacturer gains are unverified.

parameters.name: Public and observation access separation
parameters.relationship: Public and observation visitors need security separation from tenant groups; dedicated shuttles or separate sky-lobby entrances add shafts but protect tenant lifts and support public uses high in the tower.

parameters.name: Secured floors and stair re-entry
parameters.relationship: Security zoning that locks stair doors against entry is limited: an unlocked re-entry door must lie within 2 storeys (3.4.6.18.(1)); maglocks only into a public corridor or area the Chief Building Official accepts.

parameters.name: Regulator acceptance for novel systems
parameters.relationship: Double-deck, multi-car and ropeless options may need acceptance by Technical Safety BC; its page is silent on them, so the tool flags 'regulator acceptance required' until confirmed.

parameters.name: Evacuation-lift option
parameters.relationship: Occupant-evacuation lifts could shorten evacuation of a 250-300 m tower; CIBSE Guide D chapter 6 covers them, but no Canadian requirement was retrieved. Linked to P11-M08; unresolved.

metrics.name: Total core shaft area vs single-deck baseline at equal service
metrics.good: lower than baseline with all P11-M01 bands green or amber
metrics.bad: saving achieved only by a red P11-M01 band
metrics.basis: [applicability: project_example] No universal saving percentage found; Peters reports option-specific charts only. Uses total core.
metrics.method: sum of total core footprints per option

metrics.name: Double-deck floor-height uniformity
metrics.good: green: all stopped floors equal height
metrics.bad: red: any stopped floor differs without an adjustable-spacing cab
metrics.basis: [applicability: engineering_principle] Stated by Peters (UK practice): all floors must be equal height for double-deck cabs.
metrics.method: compare storey heights at served floors

metrics.name: Destination-control waiting time vs nominated interval
metrics.good: green: AWT <= 0.8 x nominated interval
metrics.basis: [applicability: institutional] UQ DS-11 (Australia), not code. v1 badge: simulation not performed; roadmap.
metrics.method: Roadmap: simulated average waiting time / nominated interval

metrics.name: Transfers per typical trip (design-intent switch)
metrics.good: no pass/fail: direct (0) or one transfer to a public sky room, chosen by the team
metrics.basis: [applicability: uk_guidance] Direct travel is a London speculative-office criterion (Stopes); Vancouver market and VTC jury preference are unsourced.
metrics.method: count lift changes on the path lobby to floor

metrics.name: Firefighter elevator changes to reach any floor
metrics.good: green: changes <= 1
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 3.2.6.5.(5) agree; BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025 unread, show 'edition check pending'. Add 'requires AHJ agreement' with passenger double-deck.
metrics.method: graph search on shaft and lobby connectivity

metrics.name: Firefighter elevator run time to top served floor
metrics.good: green: <= 60 (900 kg load)
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 3.2.6.5.(2) agree (1 min). At 244-305 m this sets a minimum speed for the firefighter shaft or a change floor. VBBL 2025 unread.
metrics.method: run time from the speed profile over the distance from the firefighter entrance level

metrics.name: Recall time to firefighter entrance or transfer lobby
metrics.good: green: each elevator <= 300 s (simultaneous-operation rule waived)
metrics.bad: amber: > 300 s; generator must carry firefighter elevators plus one at once (3.2.7.9.(2))
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] VBBL 2019 3.2.7.9.(3) only; VBBL 2007 not read for this clause; VBBL 2025 unread.
metrics.method: run time from most remote storey to entrance or transfer lobby per group

metrics.name: Non-coincident stop share (double-deck figure of merit)
metrics.good: high (no sourced threshold)
metrics.basis: [applicability: project_example] Defined by Peters; no limit stated. Roadmap with double-deck.
metrics.method: Monte Carlo with odd/even floor restriction (roadmap)

modules.method: For each option, re-run P11-M01 using total core. Single-deck: N rises by floors per rise. Sky lobby: shuttle group plus local groups, transfer floors flagged, express term included. Rank options by total core area subject to P11-M01 bands not red. Compute transfers per journey (design-intent switch), firefighter-elevator changes and run time, recall time to the entrance or transfer lobby, secured-floor re-entry spacing and public-floor access. Double-deck and destination dispatch are roadmap: their round-trip formulas were not retrieved, so implement from the worked cases in P11-S23 and validate before showing pass/fail.
visualization: Side-by-side rise diagrams per option with transfer floors marked
Stacked bar of total core shaft area by level for each option
Badge row (floor-height equality, firefighter reach, run time, recall time, regulator acceptance) linked to source
Sky-lobby floors drawn on the 3D tower with an annotation for public-room potential
modules.human_judgment: Trade-off between core efficiency, direct travel and public-room potential; transfer acceptability for public users; security separation; vendor-neutral choice of double-deck or multi-car; authority agreement for a shared firefighter lift.
modules.limits: Double-deck and shuttle formulas not retrieved. Destination dispatch gains (25-30%, P11-S33) are unverified marketing figures. No Canadian precedent found for sky-lobby transfers.

modules.name: Mechanical floors, plant space, risers and emergency power
modules.design_question: How many plant floors, where, and how much plant, electrical, emergency-generator and riser area does the tower need, and how do they shape the silhouette and public-facing floors?
modules.effort: M: about 7 person-days (5 for plant, risers and pressure zones; 2 for the emergency-power node). 10 Dec release, not in the 13 Nov cut.
inputs: Layer 0: tower height, storey heights, program areas by tag (mechanical tag = existing plant)
Plant capacities and electrical demand from P11-M04
Lift overrun, pit and machine-room needs from P11-M01 and P11-M02; firefighter elevator count and RecallTimeByGroup from P11-M02
Outrigger or transfer floors from the structure module
User presets: hydronic rating, pipe and valve rating, minimum residual water pressure, air-handling reach, area per kW, lift motor kW, smoke-control and venting fan kW, fire pump kW
outputs: PlantFloorSchedule {level, function, area m2, floor height} with a minimum-to-maximum floor count
DomesticWaterZoneTable {zone, level range, static head kPa, PRV station}
RiserAllocation {riser type, area per level, core or perimeter}
EmergencyLoad {item, kW, runtime h, clause} and GeneratorAndFuelSpace (m2)
ElectricalSpaceEstimate {transformer, switchroom, radio equipment room m2}
PlantShare (information only) and LouvreZones for the facade module

parameters.name: Domestic-water zone height and PRV stations
parameters.relationship: Static head is 9.81 kPa per m. Static pressure at any fixture is limited to 550 kPa by a PRV (VPBL 2019 2.6.3.3). Downfeed zone height = (550 - P_min) / 9.81; branch PRVs allow taller risers up to pipe rating.

parameters.name: Minimum residual pressure at top fixture
parameters.relationship: Preset 140 kPa (about 20 psi, which a trade article says codes often use); 275 kPa (40 psi) is the comfort option. A lower P_min lengthens zones and cuts PRV stations.

parameters.name: Pipe, valve and pump pressure rating
parameters.relationship: Rating caps riser pressure where branch PRVs replace zone stations, setting how many zones a tower of 244-305 m needs. Editable preset; no sourced value.

parameters.name: Hydronic pressure break (equipment rating)
parameters.relationship: Chilled and heating water static head also rises 9.81 kPa per m; above the rating of exchangers, chillers or coils a heat-exchanger break at a plant floor is needed. Rating is an editable team preset.

parameters.name: Air-handling reach and riser congestion
parameters.relationship: Duct reach, shaft area and damper count limit how many floors one plant floor serves; shorter reach adds plant floors and louvred bands on the facade. Reach is an editable preset.

parameters.name: Plant-floor frequency (sanity range)
parameters.relationship: A weak tertiary rule gives about one plant floor per ten tenant floors; more frequent plant shortens risers but removes lettable or public floors and adds louvres. Information range only.

parameters.name: Heavy plant location (generators, chillers)
parameters.relationship: Heavy plant at the top forces goods-lift capacity and riser routes to match; at 22 Bishopsgate one goods lift still needed a 7,400 kg special operation.

parameters.name: Top-floor competition (plant vs public/observation)
parameters.relationship: Plant, viewing gallery and restaurant compete for top floors; at 22 Bishopsgate not every goods lift could serve every top floor.

parameters.name: Electrical room, substation and generator area
parameters.relationship: Peak demand from P11-M04 sets transformer and switchroom area through area-per-kW presets; heavy items drive goods-lift capacity and routes for plant replacement.

parameters.name: Emergency generator load and runtime
parameters.relationship: A generator must run at full load at least 2 h for every elevator above the first storey, power-dependent firefighting water, stair air-quality and venting fans (3.2.7.9.(1)); firefighter elevators plus one more at once unless recall takes 5 min or less.

parameters.name: Emergency conductor protection
parameters.relationship: Emergency, fire-pump and fire-alarm conductors need 1 h protection; conductors for smoke-management systems need 2 h (3.2.7.10), setting protected riser or rated-cable routes through the core.

parameters.name: Alarm-live corridor make-up air and radio riser
parameters.relationship: Group C corridor make-up air must keep running on alarm (3.2.6.2.(6)); the radio antenna system (3.2.5.20) needs equipment space and risers reaching stairs, hoistways and plant rooms.

metrics.name: Plant floors as share of total floors
metrics.good: information only: observed range 7 to 26%
metrics.basis: [applicability: team] About 10% rule of thumb from a tertiary source (Wikipedia, citations needed); a range until a CTBUH or engineering source is found.

metrics.name: Domestic-water static head per PRV zone
metrics.good: green: pressure at lowest fixture <= 550 and residual at top fixture >= P_min preset
metrics.bad: red: > 550 without a PRV, or residual below preset
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] VPBL 2019 2.6.3.3 (consolidated 23 Jan 2024); VBBL 2025 Book II (NPC 2020-based) unread. r1 formula 550 / 9.81 ignored residual pressure; P_min is a trade-source preset.
metrics.method: zone height x 9.81 within the window P_min to 550

metrics.name: Hydronic static head vs equipment rating
metrics.good: green: static head <= rating preset
metrics.basis: [applicability: team] Rating preset is a team assumption; typical commercial ratings not sourced.

metrics.name: Plant-floor count range
metrics.good: report minimum to maximum; user selects
metrics.bad: single value shown without a range
metrics.basis: [applicability: team] Minimum from the larger of hydronic and air-handling needs; maximum from their sum; range reflects unsourced presets.

metrics.name: Plant area as share of GFA
metrics.good: lowest consistent with P11-M04 sizing

parameters.name: Height of top-storey floor above grade
parameters.relationship: Subsection 3.2.6 applies above 18 m to the uppermost floor of the top storey for every group (3.2.6.1.(1)(a)); 3.2.7.9 emergency power uses the same 18 m. A 244-305 m tower triggers all, so the module records clause and edition.

parameters.name: Major occupancy mix and sprinklers
parameters.relationship: From M09. The strictest occupancy governs (3.2.2.6); sprinklers throughout to NFPA 13 (3.2.2.18.(3), 3.2.5.12), standpipes 3.2.5.8-3.2.5.11, fire pump to NFPA 20 (3.2.5.18). Mixed use must satisfy the strictest combination.

parameters.name: Firefighter elevator layout
parameters.relationship: One elevator: 2.2 m2, 900 kg, top floor in 1 min, at most one change, closure and enclosure per 3.2.6.5; safety facilities near the firefighters' entrance (3.2.5.19). Constrains zoned and sky-lobby lift schemes.

parameters.name: Stair smoke control by location
parameters.relationship: Stairs above the lowest exit level need a bottom vent of 0.05 m2 per door, at least 1.8 m2. Stairs below it, including transit-link stairs, hold contamination to 1% over 2 h (3.2.6.2.(2)); the Notes give a deemed-to-comply route.

parameters.name: Smoke from below the lowest exit storey (3.2.6.2.(4))
parameters.relationship: Hoistways and shafts passing the lowest exit storey need vestibules, seals or vents so below-grade fire smoke does not reach upper floors; transit and parking levels drive this. Vent area follows height curves in the Notes.

parameters.name: Connected buildings and underground walkway
parameters.relationship: 3.2.6.3 limits contaminated air between connected buildings (vestibule vented or pressurised); 3.2.3.20: 1 h separation, smoke-barrier doors every 100 m or 1.5x travel limit, 9 m width; 3.2.4.2.(6): separate alarm treatment. Consultant decides applicability.

parameters.name: Elevator recall and building-services controls
parameters.relationship: Automatic and manual recall with detectors at lobbies, hoistway and machine room, to an alternate floor (3.2.6.4); fans stoppable at the central facility (3.2.6.2.(5)); Group C corridor make-up air stays on (3.2.6.2.(6)).

parameters.name: Emergency power and radio system
parameters.relationship: 2 h generator for lifts, firefighting water and smoke fans (3.2.7.9); 1 h conductor protection, 2 h for smoke management (3.2.7.10); radio antenna with 98% coverage in stairs, lobbies, hoistways and plant rooms (3.2.5.20).

parameters.name: Alternative-solution path
parameters.relationship: Non-compliance needs an alternative solution meeting at least Division B performance (Division A 1.2.1.1.(1)(b), applied by the Appeal Board); the register records rationale the VTC jury may weigh as a justified breach.

parameters.name: Occupant load factor per use
parameters.relationship: Load = area / Table 3.1.17.1: office 9.30, personal services 4.60, mercantile 3.70 (basement, first storey) or 5.60, dining 1.20, standing 0.40, garage 46.00, public corridor 3.70; 2 persons per dwelling-unit sleeping room. Denser uses widen stairs.

parameters.name: Exit width per person
parameters.relationship: Width = load x 8 mm (stairs rise <= 180, run >= 280), 9.2 mm (steeper stairs, ramps over 1:8) or 6.1 mm (doors, corridors, gentle ramps). Each exit counts for at most half the required width.

parameters.name: Minimum clear width (Table 3.4.3.2.-A)
parameters.relationship: Stairs 900 mm if serving not more than 2 storeys above or 1 below the lowest exit level, else 1100 mm; corridors 1100; doorways 800. In a tall tower the 1100 mm minimum, not 8 mm per person, usually sets stair area.

parameters.name: Cumulative width
parameters.relationship: Width need not accumulate in an exit serving floors one above the other (3.4.3.2.(4)) but does at interconnected floor spaces (3.4.3.2.(6)) and where exits converge. Sizing is per storey, so stairs do not widen down the tower.

parameters.name: Number and separation of exits
parameters.relationship: At least two exits per floor area (3.4.2.1); least distance between exits is half the maximum diagonal, 9 m cap for public-corridor floors (3.4.2.3); exterior discharges 9 m apart, 6 m if sprinklered and within 15 m of a street.

parameters.name: Travel distance limit
parameters.relationship: 3.4.2.5.(1): 45 m sprinklered (tower default), 40 m business, 30 m other, 105 m public-corridor floor, 60 m garage; 50 m in a service space (3.4.2.4.(3)); underground walkway rule (3.2.3.20.(4)). Sprinkler switch from M09 picks the limit.

parameters.name: Stair flight and handrail geometry
parameters.relationship: Flight rise at most 3.7 m (3.4.6.3); stairs 1100 mm or wider need handrails on both sides plus intermediate rails so one is reachable within 750 mm (3.4.6.5); wider stairs add landing area and core size.

parameters.name: Stair re-entry (emergency crossover access)
parameters.relationship: 3.4.6.18 is the re-entry rule: stair doors may not lock against entry where travel to an unlocked door exceeds 2 storeys; maglocks only into a public corridor or an area the Chief Building Official accepts. It sets security zoning and unlocked floors.

modules.name: Smoke control, stack effect and evacuation simulation (screening)
modules.design_question: Do stack effect, stair smoke control (below and above the lowest exit level), the transit link and evacuation flows work in a 250-300 m tower, and how long would stair evacuation take?
modules.effort: L: 15+ person-days (coupling to CONTAM and JuPedSim); roadmap, after 10 Dec.
inputs: Layer 0 geometry: storeys, shafts, stairs, doors, below-grade transit-link stairs and vestibules
Smoke-control strategy and stair classification (above or below lowest exit level) from P11-M05
Stair widths and occupant loads from P11-M06
Climate: January design temperature on a 2.5% basis, preset -6 C (VBBL 2019 Table C-2); indoor 21 C team assumption
outputs: PressureProfile (Pa per storey) and neutral-plane height

parameters.name: Indoor-outdoor temperature difference and height
parameters.relationship: Stack pressure dp = g x h x (rho_out - rho_in), ideal gas. At -6 C outside and 21 C inside a 300 m shaft sees about 350 Pa end to end, about 175 Pa each end; cold weather pushes air into upper floors and shafts.

parameters.name: Below-grade stair smoke control
parameters.relationship: Stairs below the lowest exit level, including transit-link levels, must keep contamination to 1% over 2 h. The Notes' route: top vent 0.1 m2 per storey less door credits, separate shaft, 0.47 m3/s air per storey.

parameters.name: Above-grade stair bottom vent
parameters.relationship: Stairs above the lowest exit level need a bottom vent of 0.05 m2 per door, at least 1.8 m2; more doors per shaft raise vent area and ground-level openings.

parameters.name: Pressurised stairs and door forces
parameters.relationship: Mechanical pressurisation aims at least 12 Pa with two doors open (Note A-3.2.6.2.(3)); exit doors must open at no more than 90 N (3.4.6.16.(3)); research suggests 130 N. Stack effect adds load on shaft doors.

parameters.name: Smoke from the transit link and below-grade levels
parameters.relationship: A link vestibule vented to outdoors or pressurised at least 12 Pa above adjacent floors limits smoke between buildings (Note A-3.2.6.3.(1)); shaft vents follow height curves (Note A-3.2.6.2.(4)).

parameters.name: Occupant load and stair width
parameters.relationship: Higher load per stair width lengthens evacuation time and raises stair density; widths come from P11-M06.

parameters.name: Lift-assisted evacuation
parameters.relationship: Lifts for assisted or general evacuation shorten total evacuation time of a 250-300 m tower but need provisions no Canadian clause was found to set; CIBSE Guide D chapter 6.7 covers it.

metrics.name: Contamination in stairs below the lowest exit level over 2 h
metrics.good: green: <= 1
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] 3.2.6.2.(2); BCBC 2018, VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 agree; re-check VBBL 2025. Earlier 'case target' reading was wrong.

metrics.name: Above-grade stair bottom vent area
metrics.good: green: >= larger of 0.05 x doors and 1.8
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] 3.2.6.2.(3); BCBC 2018, VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 agree. Re-check VBBL 2025.

metrics.name: Door-opening force at stair doors under stack and pressurisation
metrics.good: green: <= 90
metrics.basis: [applicability: code + team interpretation] 90 N is the by-law latch-release force (3.4.6.16.(3)); applying it to stack screening is a team reading. Note cites 130 N from research.
metrics.method: stack or pressurisation dp x door area / lever arm model, then CONTAM

metrics.name: Stair pressurisation differential
metrics.good: green: >= 12 with two doors open
metrics.basis: [applicability: code] Explanatory Note A-3.2.6.2.(3) recommends a 12 Pa minimum; not a mandatory limit.

metrics.name: Stack-effect pressure difference across shaft doors (screening)
metrics.good: report neutral plane and door forces
metrics.basis: [applicability: engineering_principle] Physics gives dp from height and temperature difference; limit comes only via the 90 N door force above.

metrics.name: Total stair evacuation time
metrics.good: no sourced threshold (user target)
metrics.basis: [applicability: team] No Canadian threshold found; report the curve only.

modules.method: Build a multizone airflow network in CONTAM from storeys, shafts and leakage presets; compute stack pressures at -6 C. Test below-grade stair venting or pressurisation against 1% over 2 h, above-grade stairs against the vent rule, and the transit-link vestibule against the 12 Pa and vent options. Check door forces against 90 N. Run JuPedSim on the stair geometry with P11-M06 loads for evacuation time and density maps, with and without lift-assisted evacuation. Present all results as screening for the fire engineer. Leakage areas, fan data and walking speeds are editable presets with no sourced values.
visualization: Vertical pressure-profile plot (storey vs Pa) with neutral plane marked
Stair-density animation over the stair plan
Evacuated-persons-vs-time curve
Badges: below-grade 1% over 2 h, above-grade vent area, link vestibule, each linked to by-law text and Note
modules.human_judgment: Fire engineering, evacuation strategy, tenability criteria and authority acceptance.
modules.limits: CONTAM's GUI is Windows-only (engine runs on Linux). Leakage, fan and walking-speed presets are unsourced. No CFD. Screening for an ideas competition, not engineering design.

sources.extract: Lists VBBL 2019, Vancouver Plumbing By-law 2019, VBBL 2014 and VBBL 2007 as Vancouver items; no VBBL 2025. VBBL 2025 must be downloaded from the City by hand.

flags.claim: Canadian and Vancouver codes require refuge floors (as in some Asian jurisdictions) in supertall towers.
flags.correction: No refuge-floor clause appears among the 3.2.6 requirements in the 2024 BC Part 3 checklists or the VBBL 2007 text. Treat refuge floors as an alternative-solution option.
flags.detail: Evidence: P11-S04, S05, S44. r2: VBBL 2019 3.2.6 has none either (P11-S63) and 3.3.3.6 'Areas of Refuge' is about treatment compartments (P11-S64). The 3.3.1.7 protected-zone pointer is corrected in an r2 flag.

flags.claim: CIBSE Guide D (2015) provides the current lift-design criteria.
flags.correction: The 2015 edition is superseded by the 2020 edition; the portal also lists 2025 Guide D items of unconfirmed status.
flags.detail: Source P11-S28. Lift criteria here come from papers and standards citing Guide D, so values must be checked against the current edition before submission.

flags.claim: BCBC 2024, with its adaptable-unit rule from 10 March 2025 and the provincial Zero Carbon and Energy Step Codes, is the confirmed governing code for the Vancouver site, and these thresholds are verified.
flags.correction: VBBL 2025 (By-law 14343, in force 15 September 2025, base text BCBC 2024 as amended) governs. Provincial-only rules are shown as reference with Vancouver applicability unverified.
flags.detail: The BC Codes 2024 page says BC Codes do not apply in Vancouver (P11-S01). Vancouver limits come from VBBL Part 10 and the rezoning policy. VBBL 2025 text unread.

flags.claim: The 1% contaminated air over 2 h stair target is only a design target from BCAB 1844's facts, not a code limit, and it applies to the tower's exit stairs.
flags.correction: It is a code performance requirement, Sentence 3.2.6.2.(2), for exit stairs serving storeys below the lowest exit level (including transit-link levels), at the January 2.5% design temperature. Stairs above get the bottom vent (0.05 m2 per door, minimum 1.8 m2).
flags.detail: Confirmed by BCAB 1844 (P11-S09), VBBL 2007 (P11-S44) and, in r2, VBBL 2019 (P11-S63). Re-check numbering in BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025.

flags.claim: RTT = 2H*tv + (S+1)*ts + 2P*tp is the general-analysis form used in P11-S23, and is valid for every rise of a supertall.
flags.correction: P11-S23 prints no such equation. The formula is the classic equal-floor form with no express-jump term and P undefined. The engine uses general analysis with a kinematic express term and P = average car load.
flags.detail: Peters 2000 (P11-S54, abstract only) introduces an express zone term. Unit tests against the Peters worked example and the Arup rises are required before any gauge shows pass/fail.

flags.claim: No refuge-type provision exists, so any refuge or waiting area is purely a design choice.
flags.correction: Keep 'no mandatory refuge floor'. r1 added 3.3.1.7 protected zones to the checklist; r2 note: 3.3.1.7 is deleted in Vancouver, so see the r2 flag. Keep an evacuation-elevator item.
flags.detail: Evidence: P11-S04, S05 (provincial checklists), S48 and, in r2, S64 (VBBL 2019 '3.3.1.7. Deleted.'). The r1 correction was itself wrong for Vancouver.

flags.claim: The maximum travel distance for each occupancy is set in 3.4.2.4.
flags.correction: Limit values sit in 3.4.2.5 (location of exits); 3.4.2.4 covers measurement and the 50 m service-space case; 3.3.1.6 covers travel within suites. The sprinkler switch selects the limit.
flags.detail: VBBL 2007 (P11-S45) and VBBL 2019 (P11-S65): 45 m sprinklered, 40 m business, 30 m other, 105 m public corridor, 60 m garage. BCAB 1661 (P11-S53) confirms 45 m. VBBL 2025 unread.

flags.claim: One person per 8 m2 NIA is one of the sourced design densities on an equal footing.
flags.correction: 1 per 8 is a London speculative buffer; the developer expected about 1 per 10 on average. Default office density is 1 per 10 m2 as a team assumption, with 1 per 8 as an option.
flags.detail: Stopes (P11-S22) describes the 1 per 8 figure as a buffer and marketing benchmark.

flags.claim: A 550 kPa plumbing pressure limit forces a plant floor, break tank or reducing station about every 56 m of height.
flags.correction: The 550 kPa limit is handled by PRV stations per domestic-water zone. Plant-floor spacing follows hydronic equipment ratings, air-handling reach and riser congestion (editable presets). The 56 m figure is further corrected in an r2 flag.
flags.detail: BC Plumbing Code 6.3.3.(1) per BCAB 1454 (P11-S49) and VPBL 2019 2.6.3.3 (P11-S68); high-rise practice uses PRV stations at zone tops (P11-S52). Plant count is a range.

flags.claim: Passenger-shaft area is the lift core area, so NetToGross computed from it is meaningful.
flags.correction: Total core adds firefighter, stretcher, goods and parking lifts, lobbies, pits and overruns. Passenger-only and total are reported separately and net-to-gross uses the total.
flags.detail: Peters counts passenger shafts only (P11-S23); 22 Bishopsgate needed a 7,400 kg goods lift (P11-S22).

flags.claim: Residential and hotel lift population can be derived from area / density.
flags.correction: Residential and hotel population uses persons per dwelling by bedroom count or per room with occupancy rate; area-based density applies to offices only.
flags.detail: Arup uses 1.5 to 4.0 persons per unit (P11-S26); UQ uses persons per bedroom (P11-S25).

flags.claim: BC grid electricity is very low because 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh is its emission factor (and natural gas can be omitted from the factor table).
flags.correction: 0.011 is the Part 9 prescriptive heating-source ceiling for EL-2 to EL-4, not a factor. Electricity and natural gas factors must come from the City Energy Modelling Guidelines; presets are unverified.
flags.detail: P11-S19 states the ceiling and lists only additional fuels. Natural gas is the main fossil fuel in Vancouver Part 3 buildings, so it is added.

flags.claim: Protected zones in accessible floor areas (3.3.1.7) are a current checklist item for this tower, typically met by sprinklers.
flags.correction: Vancouver deletes the article. Mark it 'deleted in VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019, confirm VBBL 2025', make the metric information only, and keep refuge or assisted-evacuation areas as alternative-solution options tied to P11-M08.
flags.detail: VBBL 2019 Section 3.3 reads '3.3.1.7. Deleted.' (P11-S64) as did VBBL 2007 (P11-S48). The 3.8.3.19 cross-reference is 'Counters' in VBBL 2019. 3.3.3.6 'Areas of Refuge' is treatment compartments only. The 2024 BC checklists are provincial.

flags.claim: Emergency crossover access (3.4.6.18) is a different provision from stair re-entry doors (r1 text cited VBBL 2007 3.4.6.17 for re-entry).
flags.correction: In VBBL 2019, 3.4.6.18 'Emergency Crossover Access to Floor Areas' is the re-entry rule; 3.4.6.17 is 'Security for Banks and Mercantile Floor Areas'. Stair doors may not lock against entry where travel to an unlocked door exceeds 2 storeys.
flags.detail: P11-S65: maglocks only into a public corridor or an area the Chief Building Official accepts; unlocked floor must reach another exit. Conflicts with M02 security zoning. Reading of 'up or down' is a consultant question.

flags.claim: Vancouver's rules on adaptable units, power door operators, tactile indicators and accessible hotel rooms are unknown, so only provincial BCBC 2024 references can be shown.
flags.correction: Base M07 on VBBL 2019 Section 3.8: 3.8.5.1 adaptable units, 3.8.2.7 power doors, 3.8.2.10 tactile indicators, 3.8.2.12 hotel rooms (1 per 40, plus 1 per 20 with visual alarm). Show provincial rules only as comparison.
flags.detail: P11-S67 (consolidated 7 Mar 2023). Adult changing tables and BC adaptable 'large building' threshold are not in VBBL 2019. VBBL 2025 unread.

flags.claim: The domestic-water pressure zone height is 550 kPa / 9.81 kPa per m, about 56 m.
flags.correction: Zone height = (P_max - P_min_residual) / 9.81 for downfeed zones, with a branch-PRV option limited by pipe and valve ratings. Cite VPBL 2019 Book II 2.6.3.3, check VBBL 2025 Book II.
flags.detail: The by-law limits static pressure at any fixture to 550 kPa (P11-S68); a zone also needs residual pressure at its top fixture. Trade source uses a 30 psi differential (P11-S52). P_min presets are team assumptions.

flags.claim: A single Table 10.2.2.5.A1 row (office, hotel or Group C) is the limit to test the tower's GHGI, TEUI and TEDI against.
flags.correction: Use an area-weighted composite from M09 areas (method per City guidelines Section 5, unread), and offer Table B, Table C and the Passive House route as selectable paths.
flags.detail: Note (1) to Table A1 sends multiple occupancies to Section 5 of the guidelines; 'other occupancies' use a GHGI-only reference rule (P11-S43).

flags.claim: The Vancouver January 2.5% design temperature for 3.2.6.2.(2) has not been retrieved and must be a user entry.
flags.correction: Preset -6 C (1% = -8 C) from VBBL 2019 Table C-2; future rows -4 C (2020s) and -2 C (2050s). Re-check VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: P11-S69 (Appendix C, consolidated 1 Jan 2021, explanatory). July 2.5% dry bulb 28/30/32 C.

flags.claim: VBBL 2007 is the most recent Vancouver Part 3 text that can be read, so its values are the presets.
flags.correction: Re-stamp presets to VBBL 2019 (Part 3 to 1 Jul 2024; Section 3.5 to 1 Jan 2021; Section 3.8 to 7 Mar 2023) and download VBBL 2025 by hand. VBBL 2007 stays in the edition map only.
flags.detail: P11-S62 to S70 opened in r2; values checked were unchanged from VBBL 2007.

flags.claim: Sprinkler status can be switched off per storey as a legitimate option for a 244-305 m tower.
flags.correction: Lock sprinklers to 'required' (NFPA 13); an 'off' entry is only a flagged alternative solution.
flags.detail: VBBL 2019 3.2.2.18.(3) requires every new building to be sprinklered and the any-height articles 3.2.2.20, .23, .29, .47, .55, .64, .80 require sprinklers throughout (P11-S63).

flags.claim: The high-building ruler needs both an 18 m and a 36 m trigger line, because the NBC 36 m rule might apply to Groups A, D, E and F.
flags.correction: Draw only the 18 m Vancouver line; keep the 36 m NBC rule in the edition map.
flags.detail: VBBL 2019 3.2.6.1.(1)(a) (P11-S63) and VBBL 2007 (P11-S44) use 18 m to the uppermost floor level of the top storey for every group.

flags.claim: VBBL 2025 (By-law 14343, effective 15 September 2025, based on BCBC 2024) is the governing Vancouver by-law, with seismic provisions applying to permits from 15 September 2026.
flags.detail: Effective date confirmed by a BCIT guide (P11-S50, secondary); adoption date, base code and seismic deferral come from unopened City summaries (P11-S12, S13, S14). Not on the free BC Publications site (P11-S71).

flags.claim: The 3.2.6.1 triggers apply unchanged in BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: r2: VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 use 18 m for every group (P11-S44, S63); the NBC 36 m rule is not a Vancouver value. BCBC 2024 clause (d), Group C above 18 m, is in BCAB 1930. VBBL 2025 text unread.

flags.claim: Office occupant-load factor of 9.3 m2 per person, a minimum of two exits per floor, occupancy-specific travel limits and 1100 mm minimum stair width apply in current Vancouver code.
flags.detail: r2: confirmed in VBBL 2019 (P11-S62, S65) and VBBL 2007 (P11-S45, S47) with equal values. VBBL 2025 and BCBC 2024 unread; presets carry edition stamps.

flags.claim: A 550 kPa static pressure limit applies to plumbing in a Vancouver tower.
flags.detail: r2: VPBL 2019 2.6.3.3 (P11-S68) limits static pressure at any fixture to 550 kPa by PRV. VBBL 2025 Book II (NPC 2020-based, P11-S50) unread. It sets PRV zones, not plant floors.

flags.claim: Destination dispatch cuts trip times by 25% and raises capacity by about 30%.
flags.detail: Manufacturer marketing claim cited on a Wikipedia page (P11-S33). Not used as a threshold; simulation must show the benefit.

flags.claim: Stair smoke tenability of at most 1% contaminated air by volume over 2 hours, and stair-bottom vent area of at least 0.05 m2 per door (minimum 1.8 m2), apply in current Vancouver and BC codes.
flags.detail: Superseded in r1: both are code requirements (3.2.6.2.(2) and (3)) in BCBC 2018, VBBL 2007 and, r2, VBBL 2019. 2024 and 2025 numbering unread.

flags.claim: Firefighter elevator needs 900 kg, 2.2 m2 platform, 60 s run to the top served floor, at most one elevator change and a 1 h shaft-opening closure.
flags.detail: r2: VBBL 2019 3.2.6.5 (P11-S63) matches VBBL 2007 (P11-S44). Closure and enclosure read as (a), (b) or (c); combination is interpretation. BCBC 2024 and VBBL 2025 unread.

flags.claim: Vancouver Part 3 limits are office TEUI 100, TEDI 20, GHGI 3.0; Group C over 6 storeys 120, 30, 3.0; hotel 140, 20, 4.0 kgCO2e/m2a.
flags.detail: r2: re-read in VBBL 2019 Table 10.2.2.5.A1 (to 27 Feb 2025, P11-S43). Tables B and C and the Passive House path added. VBBL 2025 Part 10 unread (P11-S61 HTTP 403); a 2022 council summary says tighter 2025 limits were proposed.

flags.claim: Natural gas emits 0.179 and BC grid electricity 0.011 kgCO2e/kWh in Vancouver compliance modelling.
flags.detail: Recalled from BC practice, not opened. Must be read from the City Energy Modelling Guidelines v3.0 (P11-S58, HTTP 403) before any compliance-style figure is shown.

flags.claim: The tower will be a rezoning, so the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings and the Higher Buildings Policy apply in addition to the by-law.
flags.detail: Inferred from the VTC brief (9.0 FSR non-residential, 244-305 m). Policy text unread (P11-S57 summary only).

flags.claim: The below-grade transit link makes the tower a connected building under 3.2.6.3.
flags.detail: r2: 3.2.6.3 exists in VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 (P11-S44, S63); 3.2.3.20 underground walkway and 3.2.4.2.(6) alarm treatment also apply to links. Absent from 2024 checklists (P11-S05) without explanation. Applicability to the VTC link needs a code consultant.

flags.claim: The Appendix C seismic and wind values for Vancouver (Sa(0.2) 0.848, PGA 0.369, hourly wind 1/50 0.45 kPa) are the hazard inputs for lift flags in VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: Table C-2 and C-3 (consolidated 1 Jan 2021, explanatory, NBC 2015 hazard model, P11-S69). BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025 hazard values unread; used as context only.

flags.claim: The 3.2.3.20 underground walkway rules and the 3.8.2.2.(5) accessible-walkway rule apply to the VTC below-grade transit link.
flags.detail: Clauses read in VBBL 2019 (P11-S63, S67). Whether the link is an 'underground walkway' or 'walkway or pedestrian bridge' is a consultant and authority question; station ownership may change it.

flags.claim: Plant floors are about 10% of total floors (information range 7 to 26%).
flags.detail: Weak rule of thumb from a tertiary source (P11-S31). Shown as an information range with no pass/fail colouring.

flags.claim: Hotel, cultural, observation and public-use lift criteria; transfers per trip as a design-intent switch; at least two accessible lifts per group.
flags.detail: No sourced figures found. Editable presets; the direct-travel preference comes from a London expectation (P11-S22), not Vancouver.

flags.claim: Default office density is 1 person per 10 m2 NIA at 80% utilisation.
flags.detail: Stopes expected about 1 per 10 on average and treats 1 per 8 as a buffer (P11-S22); UQ uses 1 per 12 (P11-S25). Editable.

flags.claim: Hydronic equipment pressure rating and air-handling reach presets set the plant-floor count range.
flags.detail: No sourced ratings or reach found. Presets are editable and the count is shown as a range.

flags.claim: Program tags map to occupancy groups as in the preset table (office D, retail E, residential and hotel C, assembly A, parking F-3).
flags.detail: r2: sprinklers are no longer an assumption (3.2.2.18.(3) requires them; see r2 FALSE_ASSUMPTION flag). Mapping remains a preset; code consultant decides. Group names follow Table 3.1.2.1 (P11-S62).

flags.claim: Transit mode share, station peak flow and escalator capacity are user entries.
flags.detail: No TransLink or CIBSE Guide D escalator figures sourced; PeakDemandByEntrance uses these entries only.

flags.claim: Minimum residual water pressure at the top fixture is 140 kPa (comfort option 275 kPa) and pipe, valve and pump rating is a preset.
flags.detail: Only a trade article (P11-S52: codes often use 20 psi, 40 psi recommended); VPBL 2019 Section 2.6 has no minimum clause. Editable presets.

flags.claim: The mixed-use energy limit is an area-weighted average of Table A1 rows using M09 areas.
flags.detail: Placeholder for City guidelines Section 5 (unread, HTTP 403). 'Other occupancies' rows use a GHGI-only reference rule and are flagged, not averaged.

flags.claim: The 90 N exit-door force is used as the stack-effect door screening limit, with 21 C indoor temperature.
flags.detail: 90 N is the latch-release force in 3.4.6.16.(3) (P11-S65); Note cites 130 N from research (P11-S70). Stack estimate about 350 Pa over 300 m is a team calculation.

flags.claim: Lift motor, smoke-control fan and fire pump kW presets size the emergency generator.
flags.detail: No sourced kW values. The 2 h runtime and the loads list are from VBBL 2019 3.2.7.9 (P11-S63); kW and fuel area per kW are editable presets.

flags.claim: P11 effort is about 52-57 person-days; the 13 Nov cut is about 16 (M09 2, M06 5, M05 3, M01 6) and 10 Dec carries about 36-41.
flags.detail: Team estimates for two students with 12 other categories; not sourced. If capacity falls short, drop M02 before M07.

flags.claim: Numeric Part 3 GHG intensity, TEDI and TEUI limits in VBBL 2025, the Section 5 mixed-occupancy method and the Green Buildings Policy for Rezonings text.
flags.detail: VBBL 2019 Tables A1, B, C read (P11-S43); VBBL 2025 Part 10, City guidelines v3.0 and the current rezoning policy not read (HTTP 403). Download by hand before 13 Nov.

flags.claim: Firefighter elevator rated load, speed, maximum changes and shaft fire rating in BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: VBBL 2007 and VBBL 2019 agree (P11-S44, S63); VBBL 2025 Article 3.2.6.5 and any Vancouver very-tall-building additions unread.

flags.claim: Whether exit-stair width accumulates down the tower in BCBC 2024 / VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: VBBL 2007 and 2019 3.4.3.2.(4) say width need not be cumulative except interconnected floors (P11-S45, S65). Confirm in VBBL 2025; drives stair core area.

flags.claim: Vancouver rules for adaptable dwelling units, power door operators, CSA B651 tactile indicators and accessible hotel rooms in VBBL 2025.
flags.detail: r2 narrowed: VBBL 2019 Section 3.8 read (P11-S67). VBBL 2025 unread; adult changing tables and BC adaptable threshold not in VBBL 2019. Request the City rule.

flags.claim: Seismic, wind-sway, rope-length and stack-effect constraints on lifts in a Vancouver supertall, and Technical Safety BC acceptance of double-deck, multi-car or ropeless lifts.
flags.detail: CSA B44-16 in force in BC (P11-S51); seismic clause and post-earthquake availability unread. Appendix C hazard values give context only (P11-S69).

flags.claim: Current BCO Guide to Specification criteria for waiting time and time to destination.
flags.detail: BCO 2014 wording is quoted second-hand by Stopes (P11-S22); later editions not checked. UK guidance, not a Canadian requirement.

flags.claim: VBBL 2025 (By-law 14343) and the 2025 Part 10 wording have not been read; every Part 3 and Part 10 preset is an edition-stamped VBBL 2019 value.
flags.detail: vancouver.ca and bylaws.vancouver.ca return HTTP 403 to WebFetch and were not bypassed (P11-S14, S61); free.bcpublications.ca has no VBBL 2025 (P11-S71). A student must download both in a normal browser and re-check 3.2.6, 3.2.7.9, 3.3.1.7, 3.4.2.5, 3.4.3.2, 3.4.6.18, 3.8.5 and Table 10.2.2.5.A1 before 13 Nov.

flags.claim: Reading of the 3.4.6.18 distance rule: unlocked re-entry door nearest in either direction within 2 storeys, or a stricter pattern.
flags.detail: Text says travel 'up or down' to an unlocked door must not exceed 2 storeys (P11-S65). Consultant to confirm; tool shows the check with the interpretation stated.

unresolved_relationships: Optimal plant-floor spacing versus tower height: hydronic pressure breaks (equipment rating), floors served per air-handling zone and riser area share of GFA have no sourced relationship or percentage (P11-M03 uses physics for static head, editable presets and an information-only 7-26% range).

Pipe, valve and pump pressure rating and minimum residual pressure for 250-300 m domestic-water zones: only a trade article (P11-S52); VPBL 2019 2.6.3.3 gives the 550 kPa maximum; VBBL 2025 Book II (NPC 2020-based) unread.
Effect of program mix (hotel and residential small risers versus office air shafts) on riser allocation and plant area: not sourced.
Relationship between outrigger or transfer floors (structure packet) and plant-floor placement: no source found; module only snaps to supplied floors.
Emergency-generator kW presets for lifts, smoke-control fans and fire pump, and fuel storage area per kW: no sourced values; only the 2 h runtime and the loads list (VBBL 2019 3.2.7.9) are read.
Double-deck and shuttle round-trip-time formulas and non-coincident-stop benchmarks: referenced in P11-S23 but not retrieved.
